decisions.reason: Redesigning the E and L terminals changes their letterforms but does not alter the existing composition, kerning, hierarchy, or case requirements.
The E and L terminal redesign does not change the É accent derivation requirement; the separate peak-alignment instruction from the same message is already represented in this candidate's history.
The E and L terminal redesign does not change the second V's required form; the distinct second-V observation from the same message is already represented in this candidate's history.
The client explicitly treats the Hero V as the established standard and requests changes to the remaining letters, so the approved Hero V geometry remains unchanged.
This Requirement governs the shared terminal gesture of the Hero V, second V, and É accent; the source changes the separate E and L terminal treatment without modifying that shared rule.
Refining the E and L letterforms does not change the decision to use a proprietary wordmark without a separate icon or monogram.
The requested architectural E and L treatment applies the existing brand-expression principles but does not modify those principles.
The source changes black-and-white letterform geometry and does not alter the deferred champagne-gold material treatment or its role.
